basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'VERS. 1.-- Adam vero cognovit Evam, uxorem suam, quae concepit, et peperit Cain, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1.-- Adam vero cognovit Evam, uxorem suam, quae concepit, et peperit Cain, et caetera. Cain interpretatur acquisitio sive possessio, unde etymologiam ipsius exprimens mater ait: Possedi hominem per Deum. A nonnullis etiam lamentatio dicitur, eo quod post interfectum Abel interfectus sit, et poenam sui sceleris dederit.
